name: Sensory overload
summary: Sensory overload is everyday and lived-experience language for situations in which sensory input becomes overwhelming or hard to regulate; context, predictability, control, fatigue and individual sensory profile can change what is tolerable.

includes: Experiences of sensory input becoming overwhelming or distressing.
Practical environmental changes and recovery needs.
excludes: Treating sensory overload as a standalone diagnosis.
Assuming it occurs only in autism.
Assuming the same sound, light, texture or environment overloads everyone.

claims.text: Autistic-adult sensory research describes overwhelm as context-dependent and influenced by control, predictability, tolerance and the wider state of the person rather than by stimulus intensity alone.

sources.citation: MacLennan K, O'Brien S, Tavassoli T. In Our Own Words: The Complex Sensory Experiences of Autistic Adults. Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders. 2022;52(7):3061-3075.

uncertainties.question: Which environmental changes reliably reduce overload for which people without creating new access barriers or unwanted restriction?
uncertainties.why_it_matters: Sensory profiles and acceptable supports are highly individual, so group-level findings cannot select a personal intervention.
what_would_reduce_it: Co-designed studies of environmental modifications with person-defined outcomes.
Research across neurotypes, ages and settings rather than autism-only convenience samples.

perspectives.summary: Autistic adults' accounts emphasise control, predictability, tolerance and individual variation, supporting environmental fit over a simple universal stimulus threshold.

relations.note: Sensory overload is one possible lived consequence within broader sensory-processing differences.
Sensory reactivity differences are common in autism but overload is not autism-exclusive.
Some people use repetitive or sensory actions to regulate during high load.
Reduced tolerance for sensory demands can accompany reported burnout but the constructs are not interchangeable.

questions: Can noise, light, crowding, unpredictability or lack of control be changed?
Does the resource give the person control and an easy way to stop or change it?

provenance.method: Evidence-bounded content expansion for v0.9. Primary research or authoritative source checked on 2026-08-28; claims are deliberately narrower than the source and uncertainty remains explicit.
